correctness.rationale: Linearity of integration fixes the true weighted-sum functional uniquely. Equation (16) instead squares the instantaneous loss rates and splits the second objective before squaring. A concrete nonnegative rate-pair reverses the ordering under \(\int\ell\) and \(\int\ell^2\), proving that the operation is not an order-preserving rewrite of an objective value. Direct Hamiltonian differentiation of the actual weighted sum yields affine control coefficients \(S(\omega_3B_0-\lambda_1+\lambda_3)\), \(S_1[\omega_4B_1+ eta I(\lambda_4-\lambda_5)]\), and \(S_2[\omega_4B_2+\epsilon eta I(\lambda_7-\lambda_8)]\), so bounded minimizers are bang-bang except on switching surfaces. The packaged symbolic checker reproduces these identities.

value.rationale: Resource-limited optimal control is a central contribution of the source, and the article interprets weight changes as policy tradeoffs among four economic-loss objectives. The scalarization mismatch changes the units, temporal penalty geometry, and Pontryagin control law: the true weighted sum is generically bang-bang while the published quadratic problem permits smooth interior controls. Therefore the correction materially changes what the reported strategies optimize and how their weights can be interpreted, rather than merely adjusting notation.
